title: What AI game dev tool do you wish actually existed?
author: SouthernSinger5456
selftext:
AI game development is moving ridiculously fast right now, but most of the attention seems to be going toward making creation easier.

I'm more curious about all the annoying stuff that still exists around actually building and shipping a good game.

If someone could build ONE tool for you that solved a painful part of your game development process, what would you want it to do?

Not necessarily another AI game generator or an asset generator like Meshy or Autosprite. 

It could solve something before, during, or after creation.

What's something you currently do manually, struggle with, avoid doing, spend too much time on, or wish just something worked or existed?

comments.author: Sure_Excuse_8824
comments.body:
I don’t want the AI to change the game behind my back. I want Play to be the build I approved, not whatever just compiled. If it crashes, I want all of yesterday or all of today, not half. If it can’t do physics, tell me. Don’t fake a ball. I want a project file that is still mine next year.

Which is why I am building Just a Game Engine. It doesn't make dev easier. It makes make the next prompt unable to lie about the last one. That’s the painful part generators skip: *after* the toy exists - approve, cook, play that package, crash without a chimera, revise without a second author, refuse what it can’t do.

replies.author: Sure_Excuse_8824
replies.body: I don’t need Claude to play the game. I need the person who wrote the law to walk it and find the law still there. An AI harness tests whether software runs. It will pass a game that isn’t yours. That’s the failure mode I’m building against. The model proposes. The compiler only admits what you approved. Play is you instead of a bot farming the win condition.

comments.author: tabaxi_gf
comments.body: Full pipe asset generation is still the big unanswered problem.  People are posting about using astra to build and rig things but the quality of those assets are pretty bad.  With tripo or meshy it helps but that's not a full pipeline; you are missing animations to play, missing IK rigs, materials, all aspects of 3d assets that aren't quite there yet.   One thing I'd actually like now is a way for the AI tools to pick existing 3d or 2d assets from all known public domain game assets appropraitely, which would be awesome for prototyping.  I know you can also have 'claude programmer art' as prototyping but it makes it a lot harder to see than a 3d or 2d asset that's already been battle tested and looks good.
